On Thursday (18:45 CET – live updates on the TSG app and at tsg-hoffenheim.de), the team travels to the cosmopolitan city of London, where Crystal Palace await the village club. Ahead of the match, head coach Chris Ilzer and captain Oliver Baumann spoke about the league table situation, the squad’s condition and the match itself. Chris Ilzer on… … the match: “It’s going to be an exciting and challenging task. Both clubs are in a similar position in the league. Both Crystal Palace and we want to build confidence in the UEFA Europa League to take back into the league. It looks set to be an intense match. It will be important for us to get off to a good start. I expect Crystal Palace to try to win over the crowd straight away. It could get very intense. We need to play our own game. If we manage that, our chances of picking up points will improve. We’ve prepared well and are looking forward to it.” … the opposition: “There’s always a lot of debate about which league is better than the other, but it’s quite clear that the Premier League is a cut above the rest. That’s why Crystal Palace’s league position isn’t relevant. They’ve performed well in the UEFA Europa League. We’re up against an opponent with plenty of power and dynamism. Nevertheless, we want to cause them problems. We want to grow through challenges like this.” … the UEFA Europa League: “Every single match, whether in the league, the cup or the Europa League, is an opportunity. That’s where character comes to the fore. A run like this will make us stronger. Our aim is clear: we want to finish in the top 24 to reach the knockout stages. That’s why we want to pick up points here too. A match against a Premier League side is always a good opportunity for us.” … the squad situation: “It’s currently problematic and hasn’t improved. Alexander Prass is back in the league after his suspension. However, Adam Hložek is out with muscle problems. It’s a tense situation, but we want to see it as an opportunity. In Bremen, we had five debutants in one match. A situation like this can also create potential within the club. It’s a chance for the lads. We still have a very good team and are fully confident in them.” … former Crystal Palace manager Oliver Glasner: “We know each other from the Austrian league. We’re always in touch. His success at Crystal Palace was outstanding. Winning three titles is a fantastic achievement.” Oliver Baumann on… … the UEFA Europa League: “The win against Lyon did us a world of good. We’d set our sights a bit higher in the opening matches. We’ve seen that we can pick up points in the Europa League and move up the table. We’ve built up some momentum and want to put in a good performance in London too.” … Chris Richards: “I’m really looking forward to seeing him again. I saw him in America before the World Cup. That was lovely. We spoke about our journeys over the past few years.” … Premier League teams: “I’ve had the chance to play against one or two Premier League opponents before. They always have players who are individually very strong, very fast and physically robust. That’s going to be a big challenge for us. But I’m looking forward to it.” The opponent's form: The reigning Conference League champions have had a mixed start to the season. In the English Premier League, Crystal Palace are currently in a relegation spot (18th) following three consecutive defeats. In European competition, the Eagles sit 15th in the table with four points, following a win against Lech Poznań, a draw at Beşiktaş and a defeat in Lyon. Previous encounters:  Thursday’s match will be the first ever meeting between the two clubs. Here are the key facts about the reigning UEFA Conference League champions from London. Founded: 10 September 1905 Club colours: blue and red League position in 2025/26: 15th Honours: 1x UEFA Conference League, 1x FA Cup, 1x Community Shield The stadium Crystal Palace’s stadium opened in 1924 and is situated in the Selhurst neighbourhood of the borough of Croydon. The London club’s home ground currently holds around 25,000 fans, but the local council approved expansion plans a few years ago to increase its capacity. A new main stand was designed several years ago, but the redevelopment has not yet begun. Selhurst Park served as the home ground of the fictional football club AFC Richmond in the popular series Ted Lasso, which led to the club gaining international attention. Not only have Crystal Palace and the fictional AFC Richmond played home matches at Selhurst Park, but Charlton Athletic and FC Wimbledon have also played there on a temporary basis in south London. On Thursday, TSG Hoffenheim will be visiting London for the first time for a competitive match. The crest The fact that Crystal Palace features an eagle on its crest and is also nicknamed “The Eagles” is down to former manager Malcolm Allison. The Briton, who first managed Crystal Palace from 1973 to 1976 and took charge again briefly a few years later, was a great admirer of Benfica, who also feature an eagle on their crest. In the 1980s, however, Allison went on to manage Benfica’s city rivals, Sporting. The name Built in 1851 for the Great Exhibition in Hyde Park, the Crystal Palace was regarded as an architectural sensation. Three years after the exhibition, the building was dismantled and reassembled on a larger scale in south London. Staff and others involved with the Crystal Palace founded a football club in this neighbourhood, and the club was named after the building. In 1936, the imposing structure was completely destroyed by an explosion. The first titles For many decades, Crystal Palace were a classic yo-yo team, having only established themselves in the Premier League in recent years. Over the past two years, the Austrian Oliver Glasner brought the greatest successes in the club’s history to south London. In 2025, the club first won the FA Cup, and at the start of the following season they also secured the Community Shield. Last summer, just one year after their first domestic title, they won their first international title when Crystal Palace beat Rayo Vallecano to win the UEFA Conference League in the final in Leipzig. Form Oliver Glasner left Palace at the end of last season, however, and his successor, Pierre Sage, has not yet managed to generate any real sense of optimism. After nine league matches, Crystal Palace sit in the relegation zone with seven points. In the Europa League, the London side are in 15th place following a 4-0 win against Lech Poznań, a 2-2 draw against Beşiktaş and a 2-3 defeat away to Olympique Lyon. Coach Chris Ilzer’s side lost 2-0 (0-0) away to SV Werder Bremen. The goals for the Hanseatic side were scored by Niclas Füllkrug in the 57th minute and Eren Dinkci in the 82nd minute. The line-up Head coach Chris Ilzer made six changes from the team that lost in the cup to Holstein Kiel. Oliver Baumann, Natnael Abraha, Ozan Kabak, Mats Rots, Adam Daghim and Fisnik Asllani started in place of Luca Philipp, Valentin Gendrey, Robin Hranáč, Bernardo, Alexander Prass and Tim Lemperle. Baumann started in goal once again, with the back four comprising Abraha – making his Bundesliga debut – Ozan Kabak, Koki Machida and Rots. In midfield, Leon Avdullahu and Wouter Burger played in the centre, whilst Daghim and Kramarić operated on the flanks. Asllani and Hložek started up front. The match After the kick-off, the hosts had the first chance, with Füllkrug setting up Reis, who, though unmarked on the edge of the box, failed to connect properly with the ball but only narrowly missed Baumann’s goal (3’). An intense match developed between the two sides, both of whom had been knocked out of the DFB-Pokal during the week. Hoffenheim tried to dictate the play, whilst Bremen sat deep in their own half, forced back by TSG’s counter-pressing. Debutant Abraha made a notable impact on the right side of defence. Hoffenheim had more of the play, but it was SV Werder who had the second good chance on goal. In the 24th minute, Füllkrug unjustifiably claimed a foul, but Arthur, who had found himself in space, carried on playing; however, rather than shooting himself, he played the ball into the centre, where Ozan Kabak was able to clear. Two minutes later, a header from Grüll flew just over Baumann’s goal. TSG had their first chance in the 31st minute, when Hložek struck a powerful shot from 17 metres and the ball flew just over the bar. Chris Ilzer’s side dominated proceedings and had more possession. They almost took the lead in the 45th minute: Kramarić crossed to the far post, where Asllani got his head to the ball and tried to lob it over Hein, but Pieper cleared it off the line. Hoffenheim had the first chance of the second half. Hložek played a low pass inwards to Asllani, who shot after a dribble, but Regeer was able to clear with a sliding tackle. In the 53rd minute, Baumann prevented his side from falling behind. Füllkrug shot from 20 metres, but the TSG goalkeeper tipped the powerful effort round the post. SVW were now having the better of the play and took a 1–0 lead in the 57th minute. Following a long goal kick from Hein, Füllkrug used his whole body to hold off Machida and Ozan Kabak, ran several metres and hammered the ball into the net from around 14 metres. The protests from Burger and Machida – claiming that Bremen’s striker had gained possession unfairly – were to no avail. TSG fought back, launching attack after attack, but these failed to make a decisive impact. In the 71st minute, they almost equalised, but Lemperle’s cross was slightly too far out, meaning Asllani’s header went just wide of the goal. The match was decided in the 82nd minute. The TSG defence failed to clear the ball from their own penalty area. Dinkci finished perfectly, curling the ball from the left-hand side high into the far corner – unstoppable for Baumann. Match statistic: 400 Oliver Baumann continues his pursuit of records. He played his 400th Bundesliga match in a TSG shirt. What’s next A midweek fixture is on the cards ahead of the international break. On Thursday at 18:45 CET, TSG Hoffenheim travel to London to face Premier League side Crystal Palace in the UEFA Europa League. Next Sunday (8 November at 19:30 CET), TSG host FC Schalke 04. In het kader van de Europa League komt dan namelijk Omonia Nicosia op bezoek. De kampioen van Cyprus won twee van de voorgaande drie wedstrijden in het toernooi en staat daardoor op een mooie elfde plaats. N.E.C. vinden we na de heroïsche overwinning bij Dinamo Zagreb negen plaatsen lager terug.   In de vorige speelronde van de Europa League ging Omonia Nicosia met 1-4 ten onder tegen Benfica, de ploeg waartegen N.E.C. het op 21 januari gaat opnemen in De Goffert. Beide wedstrijden daarvoor werden echter gewonnen. Eerst was er een knappe 1-0 overwinning op Celta de Vigo, waarna een afgetekende 3-0 zege op het Sloveense Celje (ook een latere tegenstander van N.E.C.) volgde.    In de competitie moet de ploeg van trainer Henning Berg op dit moment zowel Apollon Limassol als AEK Larnaca boven zich dulden. Laatstgenoemde club bezorgde Omonia onlangs de eerste nederlaag van het seizoen. In de Cypriotische topper werd het 2-0 voor AEK. Afgelopen weekend werd wel met 2-0 gewonnen van AEL Limassol, de nummer vijf op de ranglijst.     In de selectie van Omonia Nicosia vinden we drie Nederlanders terug: Luuk Brouwers, Carel Eiting en Jaden Montnor. Brouwers maakte afgelopen zomer de overstap van sc Heerenveen naar Cyprus, terwijl Carel Eiting een jaar eerder al de overstap naar het mediterrane eiland waagde. De middenvelder kampt echter al lange tijd met een knieblessure en zal er donderdag dan ook niet bij zijn. Linksbuiten Jaden Montnor speelde in de jeugd van FC Utrecht en AZ en belandde na een Oostenrijks avontuur uiteindelijk op Cyprus.    N.E.C. zit qua resultaten in een lastige periode. In Europees verband werd wel gewonnen van Dinamo Zagreb, maar in de competitie wil het al even niet meer lukken. Afgelopen weekend liepen de Nijmegenaren in Heerenveen zelfs tegen een 1-0 nederlaag aan. Een goed resultaat zou daarom niet alleen prettig zijn voor de stand in de Europa League, maar ook zorgen voor een goed gevoel richting de uitwedstrijd tegen FC Utrecht, die komend weekend gespeeld wordt.   De wedstrijd van donderdag staat onder leiding van scheidsrechter Goga Kikacheishvili. De 35-jarige Georgiër krijgt daarbij hulp van vier landgenoten. David Akhvlediani en Davit Gabisonia zijn aangesteld als assistent-scheidsrechters, terwijl Bakari Bregadze fungeert als vierde official. De Spanjaard Cesar Soto Grado doet dienst als VAR en hij wordt daarbij geassisteerd door de Georgiër Aleko Aptsiauri.   Donderdagavond wordt het koud, maar in De Goffert moet het gaan koken. Dus met zijn allen achter de ploeg en samen zorgen voor wéér een mooie Europese avond. Borst vooruit, mouwen omhoog en strijden voor club en land. Forza N.E.C.! Second-half goals from Igor Matanovic and Cyriaque Irié turned the game around for SC. It was Freiburg’s substitutes who made the difference in Augsburg on Saturday afternoon. Keisuke Goto, Igor Matanovic, Vincenzo Grifo and Cyriaque Irié all played their part in a late but ultimately deserved victory over FCA. “We told the lads last night that there was a good chance their moment would come today. It was important that they were mentally ready for it. That was the key today,” said head coach Julian Schuster, delighted with the contributions of his substitutes. As in the midweek cup victory over VfL Wolfsburg, Freiburg made seven changes to their starting XI. Derry Scherhant and Jordy Makengo, both of whom had been carrying knocks recently, replaced Grifo and Christian Günter. Mio Backhaus, Lukas Kübler, Philipp Lienhart, Niklas Beste and Lucas Höler also came into the side in place of Florian Müller, Philipp Treu, Max Rosenfelder, Irié and Matanovic. Goto, who had scored twice in the cup, was also back on the bench and watched his teammates make a bright start at the sold-out WWK Arena. Just 60 seconds after kick-off, Yuito Suzuki was played through down the inside-right channel. The Augsburg defence only just managed to cut out his pass towards Höler, who was waiting completely unmarked in front of goal. A few minutes later, Scherhant went close to giving the visitors the lead with a deflected curling effort. Gregoritsch scores against his former club Augsburg head coach Manuel Baum had made four changes to his starting XI following the cup victory over SG Sonnenhof Großaspach that secured their place in the round of 16. His side initially adopted a cautious approach, although Michael Gregoritsch did register an early attempt on goal with a long-range shot that lacked the accuracy to trouble Backhaus (10’). Gregoritsch, one of three former Freiburg players on the pitch alongside Yannik Keitel and Robin Fellhauer, was also the man who put Augsburg ahead after 18 minutes. A cross from the left picked out the completely unmarked Austrian, who beat Backhaus with a first-time finish from seven metres out. As they have so often in recent weeks, Freiburg responded well to falling behind, sticking to their approach and looking for gaps in the Augsburg defence. Despite SC’s dominance, however, it was the hosts who created the next big chance. Bayern loanee Arijon Ibrahimović picked out Gregoritsch with a pass from the byline, but Backhaus managed to keep out the striker’s shot on the turn (32’). Freiburg struggle to find a way through For all their possession, Freiburg lacked a cutting edge in the first half. Increasingly sloppy passing and cheap turnovers also disrupted their play, and the score remained unchanged heading into the break. Matanovic replaced Höler at half time, and SC began the second half on the front foot against an Augsburg side sitting deep. Matthias Ginter sent a looping header towards goal early on (47’), while at the other end, Ibrahimović curled an effort from outside the box narrowly wide of Backhaus’ goal (57’). With half an hour remaining, the game had lost much of its rhythm on a difficult Augsburg pitch. Freiburg were struggling to find ideas or move the ball quickly enough in their build-up play, while the hosts offered little going forward beyond the occasional counterattack. Substitutes turn the game around Freiburg’s equaliser therefore came almost out of nowhere. Goto, who had only just come off the bench, started the move with a clever through ball. Yannik Engelhardt then poked the ball into the path of Matanovic, who fired an unstoppable shot from the edge of the penalty area to make it 1-1 (65’). The celebrations in the lively away end were dampened shortly afterwards when Freiburg were forced into an injury-related substitution. As in the midweek cup tie, it was a right-back who had to leave the pitch, with Kübler unable to continue after receiving treatment. Rosenfelder came on to replace his injured teammate. Freiburg’s substitutes were once again at the heart of the action in the closing stages. Grifo found himself in plenty of space on the left and delivered a beautifully weighted cross towards the far post, where fellow substitute Irié rose above his marker to head home from close range (85’). Freiburg’s 2-1 lead was never seriously threatened before the final whistle. Augsburg resorted to sending high balls into the box, but the SC defence stood firm, clearing their lines, winning their aerial battles and maintaining a compact shape. When referee Christian Dingert blew for full time, the players and travelling supporters celebrated a hard-fought three points. “We found it difficult for long periods today against a very dangerous opponent. That makes us all the happier to have won,” Schuster said after the game. The fixtures have been coming thick and fast for SC Freiburg this autumn. A trip to the south of France was followed by a Bundesliga home game against Bayern and a DFB-Pokal tie against second-tier VfL Wolfsburg at the Europa-Park Stadion. Now, Freiburg are back on the road for a Bundesliga clash in Augsburg. After the cup victory over Wolfsburg, Matthias Ginter was asked whether the relentless schedule was starting to take its toll. “Actually, we’re coping pretty well. But extra time would have been tough,” replied the centre-back, who, like most of the 32,000 spectators, was probably relieved to see Freiburg get the job done inside 90 minutes. Two late goals from Keisuke Goto secured victory over Wolfsburg and sent SC through to the round of 16, providing a welcome confidence boost after three games without a win. “After failing to win our last three games, it was important for us to turn this one around and get a result like that,” said head coach Julian Schuster. Back to a traditional Saturday afternoon kick-off Wednesday’s victory over the second-tier side was not without its problems, however, with Philipp Treu picking up an injury and plenty of room for improvement in Freiburg’s performance. With so little time between Bundesliga, DFB-Pokal and Conference League fixtures, there is barely an opportunity to address everything on the training ground. Nevertheless, Schuster is determined not to let those shortcomings go unaddressed. “Even though we’re short on training sessions at the moment, we want to try to improve on the things that didn’t go quite right against Wolfsburg and in our previous games.” That will be the approach when Freiburg travel to Augsburg, where they can look forward to the relative novelty of a Saturday afternoon kick-off. Christian Günter, who set up the early opener in the cup, is expecting “a real battle”. The captain believes Augsburg have improved as a footballing side this season. Like SC, the ‘Fuggerstädter’ enjoyed a spell at the top of the Bundesliga table after opening their campaign with convincing wins over Schalke (3-0) and Frankfurt (4-1). Although they have not won since, they have picked up impressive draws against FC Bayern and Bayer Leverkusen. With two days to go until the game, Freiburg are still awaiting a diagnosis on Philipp Treu, who was forced off injured against Wolfsburg. Derry Scherhant and Jordy Makengo, both of whom missed the cup tie, could be back in contention for the trip to the ninth-placed side. On Thursday evening in the principality, SC Freiburg followed up a poor first half with a markedly better performance in the second 45. However, they were unable to equalise, and the fifth-placed side in Ligue 1 added two to their lead in the closing stages to seal victory. “We didn’t start the game the way we set out to. For me, the energy was lacking. It meant that Monaco had the upper hand,” explained Julian Schuster after the final whistle, although he praised his side for their second-half display. “The reaction after the break was very good. We missed the chance to equalise, but we were much better. Monaco exploited the space that we afforded them. I think that the 3-0 scoreline flatters them.” Three changes and a vocal away end The Freiburg coaching staff made three changes to the starting XI following the narrow defeat in Leverkusen at the weekend. Lukas Kübler, Vincenzo Grifo and Max Rosenfelder replaced Philipp Treu, Derry Scherhant and the injured Philipp Lienhart. While the Monaco fans only trickled into the sparsely populated Stade Louis II, the sold-out away end made their presence felt right from the off. The 800 Freiburg fans seemed to be in good spirits and – at the very least in terms of volume – seemed to have the upper hand. On the pitch, though, the Monegasque side set the tone and managed to get into promising positions in the box on several occasions with clever, intricate passing moves. The SCF defence managed to intervene at just the right moments, and although Mathys Detourbet was in an offside position when he got a shot off in the first few minutes of the game, his effort was saved by Mio Backhaus regardless (4’). Engelhardt sustains injury Just after the quarter-of-an-hour mark, Julian Schuster was forced into making the first change of the game. Yannik Engelhardt, who had landed heavily on his hip after an aerial duel a couple of minutes beforehand, had to depart the action and was replaced by Patrick Osterhage. Shortly after that, Freiburg threatened the Monaco goal for the first time. After a set piece from the half-way line, taken by Niklas Beste, Kübler’s header went well wide of the goal (17’). As opposed to the host’s high pressing, SCF opted for a possession-based approach to get out of their own half and boost their confidence. Halfway through the first 45, the balance of play looked to have evened out, before AS Monaco upped the ante once more. Backhaus was called into action twice, first denying Mamadou Coulibaly’s shot from a tight angle (24’), before he was called into action to neutralise the threat posed by Paris Brunner (27’). Brunner opens the scoring For a long time, it looked as though SC would manage to reach the break with the scoreline intact at 0-0. However, they went into the interval trailing 1-0 after Brunner chipped the ball over Rosenfelder, sprinted past the last defender and slotted the ball past Backhaus. The second half began with some changes in personnel – Lucas Höler entered the fray in place of Yuito Suzuki – and a couple of huge chances for SCF. A Beste corner eventually landed at Kübler’s feet at the edge of the six-yard box, but his attempt to equalise from close range went begging. Freiburg remained behind after Matthias Ginter was unable to convert a rebound. Still, SC looked like a completely different side after emerging from the dressing room, putting the opposition under pressure and establishing themselves in the AS Monaco half. For their part, the home side looked to exploit the spaces left in behind the Freiburg defence on the counter and were a hair’s breadth away from taking the lead. Once again, it was a one-on-one between Brunner and Backhaus – on this occasion, the Freiburg number one managed to get the better of the Dortmund player.  Monaco extend lead Despite setting the tone, SC hadn’t managed to change the picture, nor the scoreline with twenty minutes to go until the final whistle. The eleven Freiburg players on the pitch ran and combined fluently in and around the opposition’s sixteen-yard box and had numerous set-pieces, but still only managed to create a few promising scoring chances. Even so, Monaco added to their lead in the closing stages. Following a counterattack, Ansu Fati put Backhaus to the test with a shot from the left-hand side of the penalty area. Freiburg’s keeper managed to punch the ball away, but it landed at Lamine Camara’s feet, and the midfielder fired home to make it 2-0 (83’). Fati also got his name on the scoresheet in added time to condemn SCF to a 3-0 loss. Written by Union Content Team Union stood firm away at SK Beveren despite an early second-half red card. They struggled to create chances in the first half, but Patris nevertheless put them ahead in the 44th minute. After the break, Union were reduced to ten men, but Guilherme quickly added a second goal. Beveren pulled one back, but Union held on to secure the win. Dit bericht op Instagram bekijken Een bericht gedeeld door Royale Union Saint-Gilloise (@rusg.brussels) The Brussels side started the game with confidence. Their first threat came after just three minutes. Florucz tried his luck from the right flank, but his effort found the side netting. Beveren responded a few minutes later with a cross from the flank. Koffi misjudged the flight of the ball and failed to claim it, but the danger was quickly cleared.   Beveren enjoy possession, but Union take the lead   Beveren gradually grew into the game and Margaritha fired an effort towards goal from inside the box. His shot took a deflection off Sylla’s leg and went wide. The danger was not over, however, as Boone also got a shot away in the next attacking phase. Koffi kept the score level with a superb save, tipping the ball onto the crossbar. There was still more to come: Margaritha laid the ball off, Olantunji turned and fired straight at Koffi.   Towards the end of the first half, Union regained the upper hand. Guilherme turned and played the ball out to Zeneli. The Swede managed to get the ball through to Patris with a touch of luck. Patris made no mistake, firing the ball into the back of the net to make it 0-1. Red card and another goal   The second half got off to a difficult start for Union. Aquino had only been on the pitch for five minutes when he accidentally caught Kaboré on the leg with a late challenge. Following a VAR review, the referee showed him a straight red card.   Union refused to be rattled and responded in emphatic fashion. Florucz launched an attack down the right flank before playing Patris through. Patris laid the ball off for Guilherme, who arrived at pace and fired home to double Union’s lead: 0-2.   Beveren fight back   Beveren were not ready to give up and pulled a goal back. Olantunji got past Havenaar inside the box, leaving the defender unable to intervene. This allowed Verschueren to get his shot away and curl the ball into the net. VAR reviewed the incident, but the referee saw no infringement and allowed the goal to stand: 1-2.   The goal gave the home side renewed confidence as they pushed for an equaliser. Beveren took control of possession and committed men forward in search of a leveller. However, their attacking pressure failed to produce any further clear-cut chances. Union kept the centre of the pitch well protected and regularly won the ball back.   Even in the closing stages, the home side were unable to find another way through. Union stood firm with ten men and saw out the victory to secure all three points. The result means they remain comfortably inside the top three of the league table. Written by Union Content Team Union beat Cercle Brugge 5-2 at the Duden Park. The Brussels side fell behind early on from the penalty spot and even trailed by two goals in the second half. However, in a goal-filled encounter, Union hit back with five goals to turn the game around, with Cercle having to play with ten men following a red card.   Union hosted bottom-of-the-table Cercle Brugge, who were still searching for their first win of the season. Nevertheless, the Unionistas were determined not to underestimate their opponents, especially after being held to a draw by OH Leuven in the previous round.   Cercle Strike First   The opening stages were evenly contested, with both sides pressing high and looking to find a way through. Cercle Brugge looked the more threatening team but initially failed to create any clear-cut chances. The visitors registered the first shot on target in the 16th minute.   Cercle took the lead from the penalty spot in the 22nd minute. Chibani held Ngoura for too long inside the box, leaving the referee with little hesitation before pointing to the spot. Ngoura stepped up himself and sent Koffi the wrong way to make it 1-0. Dit bericht op Instagram bekijken Een bericht gedeeld door Royale Union Saint-Gilloise (@rusg.brussels) Union needed to raise the tempo. Aquino first delivered an excellent cross towards Florucz, who just failed to get his head on the ball. Moments later, after a neat passing move, Mofokeng whipped in a fine cross for Florucz, but the Austrian's effort went straight at the goalkeeper. Chibani also tried his luck from distance, only for Coucke to produce a fine diving save. Union went into the break trailing 1-0.   Two Goals Down, Union Fight Back to Level   The second half got off to the worst possible start for Union. Cercle were ruthlessly clinical and doubled their lead just three minutes after the restart. The visitors caught Union out from a corner, and the home side failed to clear their lines. Vanzeir collected the ball near the byline and attempted to send it back into the box, but the ball deflected off Sylla and into his own net to make it 2-0.   Cercle's two-goal cushion lasted less than a minute. Florucz immediately pulled one back for Union. Played in by De Roeve, the Austrian unleashed a strike from outside the box into the bottom-left corner to make it 2-1.   Despite Union's intense pressure, Cercle managed to break forward again in the 58th minute. Ngoura raced through one-on-one with Koffi but missed the chance to restore Cercle's two-goal lead. Union hit back almost immediately. Following a throw-in, Havenaar flicked the ball on before an unmarked Sylla headed home to bring the sides level at 2-2.   Union Overwhelm Cercle   Cercle were reduced to ten men in the 64th minute when Vanzeir was shown a red card for an overly aggressive challenge on De Roeve. Union's third goal looked increasingly likely, and ten minutes later the hosts finally took the lead. Van de Perre delivered a cross, and Sylla directed a header towards Rodriguez. Rodriguez arrived too late to make contact, and Kakou inadvertently turned the ball into his own net to put Union 3-2 ahead.   Union were not finished yet and continued to pile on the pressure. Patris delivered a cross, and Mofokeng produced a looping header over the goalkeeper and into the net to make it 4-2.   Deep into stoppage time, Union added a fifth. Mofokeng delivered a superb cross, and Rodriguez calmly headed home to complete the 5-2 rout. The emphatic comeback keeps Union firmly inside the league's top three. AZ neemt het op tegen de Italiaanse grootmacht Juventus. Het duel is niet alleen een ontmoeting met een club met een rijke Europese historie, maar ook een bijzondere wedstrijd voor de gebroeders Koopmeiners. Juventus Football Club is een van de oudste voetbalclubs van Italië. De club werd opgericht in 1897 en speelt haar thuiswedstrijden in het Allianz Stadium in Turijn. De prijzenkast van De Oude Dame is goed gevuld. Juventus werd maar liefst 37 keer landskampioen en won vijftien keer de Italiaanse beker. Ook op Europees niveau heeft de club een indrukwekkend palmares, met onder meer eindzeges in de Europa Cup I, Europa Cup II en UEFA Cup. Daarnaast won Juventus de Wereldbeker. De club bracht door de jaren heen talloze grote voetballers voort. Zo maakten onder anderen Michel Platini, Zbigniew Boniek, Pavel Nedved, Zinédine Zidane, Didier Deschamps, Alessandro Del Piero en Cristiano Ronaldo deel uit van de selectie. Ook stond Juventus aan de basis van een groot deel van de Italiaanse nationale ploegen die in 1982 en 2006 wereldkampioen werden. Spelers als Dino Zoff, Claudio Gentile, Marco Tardelli, Gianluca Vialli, Gianluigi Buffon, Fabio Cannavaro en Gianluca Zambrotta droegen in die jaren het zwart-witte shirt. Italiaanse tegenstanders In de Europese geschiedenis kwam AZ al vaker Italiaanse clubs tegen. Zo stonden de Alkmaarders tegenover Internazionale, Udinese, Napoli, Lazio Roma en AS Roma. In totaal leverden deze ontmoetingen negen wedstrijden op, waarin AZ zes keer als winnaar van het veld stapte. Twee duels gingen verloren en één wedstrijd eindigde in een gelijkspel. Het laatste duel dat de Alkmaarse club speelde tegen een Italiaanse tegenstander, was de thuiswedstrijd tegen AS Roma in 2025. In een spannende wedstrijd hielden beide ploegen elkaar lange tijd in evenwicht, waarbij doelman Rome-Jayden Owusu-Oduro met enkele belangrijke reddingen zijn doel schoon hield. Invaller Troy Parrott kroonde zich in de 80ste minuut tot matchwinner door op aangeven van David Møller Wolfe de winnende treffer te maken. Troy Parrott viert zijn doelpunt tegen AS Roma. Nederlandse connecties Juventus heeft ook een lange geschiedenis met Nederlandse tegenstanders. De Italianen speelden tot dusver 26 Europese wedstrijden tegen clubs uit Nederland. Ajax, Feyenoord, PSV, FC Twente en NEC waren de opponenten. Twaalf keer trok Juventus aan het langste eind, terwijl zeven ontmoetingen in een Nederlandse overwinning eindigden. Ook Nederlandse spelers hebben in het verleden het shirt van Juventus gedragen. Onder anderen Edwin van der Sar, Matthijs de Ligt, Edgar Davids, Eljero Elia en Mohamed Ihattaren stonden bij de Italiaanse club onder contract. Ook Dean Huijsen, zoon van voormalig AZ-speler Donny Huijsen, maakte deel uit van Juventus. Hij komt inmiddels uit voor het Spaanse nationale elftal. Gebroeders Koopmeiners Een extra bijzonder tintje aan het Europese treffen is de ontmoeting tussen Peer en Teun Koopmeiners. Beide broers doorliepen de jeugdopleiding van AZ en maakten vanuit Alkmaar hun stappen richting het professionele voetbal.  Peer maakt inmiddels deel uit van de eerste selectie van AZ, terwijl Teun zijn carrière vervolgde bij Juventus, na een tussenstap bij Atalanta Bergamo. De gebroeders Koopmeiners in AZ shirts. Wedstrijdinformatie AZ trapt het duel met Juventus donderdagavond om 21:00 uur af in het AFAS Stadion. In het gehele AFAS Stadion is roken niet toegestaan, met uitzondering van de daartoe aangewezen rookplekken. De wedstrijd staat onder leiding van de Poolse scheidsrechter Damian Sylwestrzak. De arbiter wordt geassisteerd door Adam Karasewicz en Bartosz Heinig met langs de zijlijn Lukasz Kuzma. Piotr Lasyk fungeert als VAR en Tomasz Kwiatkowski is de AVAR. text: Clube do Remo vence Botafogo (RJ) por 2 a 1 Clube Esportes Notícias Imprensa Transparência Ouvidoria Contato Newsletter Loja 🇧🇷 Clube do Remo vence Botafogo (RJ) por 2 a 1 Q uinta-feira, 29/10/2026 Por Victor Miranda A noite desta quarta-feira (28), foi de vitória para o Clube do Remo no Brasileirão 2026. A equipe azulina derrotou o Botafogo (RJ) por 2 a 1, no estádio Mangueirão. Com o resultado, o Leão chegou aos 29 pontos na Série A do Campeonato Brasileiro. A partida começou com o Remo pressionando a equipe carioca, principalmente pelo lado direito de ataque com os cruzamentos do lateral Marcelinho. Logo aos 7' de jogo, após cruzamento vindo da direita, o atacante Jajá aproveitou a sobra e marcou seu 9º gol na Série A 2026. Durante todo o primeiro tempo, o Remo foi melhor, atacando pelas pontas e levando perigo ao goleiro do Botafogo. No segundo tempo, o Remo voltou pressionando e com a posse de bola. Aos 8', após passe de Taliari, Leonel Picco chutou a bola no ângulo e marcou o segundo gol da equipe azulina. Após ampliar o placar, o Leão seguiu com o controle da partida e sem levar pressão do time adversário. O goleiro Marcelo Rangel foi fazer uma defesa no final da partida. O Botafogo diminuiu o placar quase aos 40. Com a vitória, o Remo diminuiu a distância para sair da zona de rebaixamento, o Leão encara na 34ª a equipe do Palmeiras (SP), em São Paulo, na próxima quinta-feira (05).
